observations.claim: In the screened simple compile-error cases, compiler and test feedback was sufficient; semantic evidence was not shown to add decision value.
Effect summaries exposed wrapper shapes that agents used while preserving Either and generic F[Option[...]] contracts in small prompted repairs.
Correct effect summaries were insufficient to choose between competing local APIs; the public method contract and tests remained decisive.
In small prompted cases, non-exact reconciliation states were treated as evidence rather than exact symbol-identity proof.
Tool availability did not reliably cause spontaneous semantic-tool selection across the screened sessions.

limitations: No randomized assignment or statistical power analysis.
Prompt wording, client behavior, and environment varied across the inventory.
Human interpretation was used for semantic and intent assessments.
The aggregate does not prove superiority over compiler/test or IDE/LSP baselines.
Historical raw transcripts and controller captures are not part of the public subset.
